text:
Hi Arisha,

I hope you are well.

Ahead of our meeting next week, I wanted to share two current issues we are
experiencing with Encord so that you can prepare accordingly and, if
needed, involve any relevant colleagues.

First, we are currently facing significant performance issues in Encord. In
particular, the loading times for individual studies have worsened
noticeably over the past few weeks. We are also seeing delays or issues at
times when saving labels or approving tasks. In some of these situations,
the message “High traffic detected” appears.

Second, we have a workflow-related issue concerning our reviewer Marius. In
his projects, he often has to work in two separate windows at the same
time, and it seems that in this setup labels are occasionally not being
saved properly. This specifically affects the following projects:

   -

   ICRS_New_Dataset3
   -

   ICRS_New_Dataset2
   -

   ICRS_New_Dataset1

It would be great if you could look into these topics before our meeting.
And if helpful, please feel free to invite anyone else from your team who
should be involved in the discussion.

Best regards,

Patrick

subject: RE: Encord - commercial proposal + catch-up on Monday
text:
Encord Team,

Thank you for sharing the Order Form. We're close on the overall scope and are excited about the potential partnership. Before moving forward, we'd like to propose a set of revisions to better align with our operational requirements and standard procurement practices.

Below are some key proposed changes:

1. Payment Structure & Financial Risk
Current: 100% annual fee invoiced upfront
Proposed Revision:

  *   Move to quarterly billing or milestone-based payments tied to delivery and/or meeting performance benchmarks
  *   Introduce a 10-20% holdback tied to compliance and acceptance criteria
  *   Include a refund or credit mechanism for undelivered or non-conforming services
2. Service Levels & Performance Metrics
Current: "Commercially reasonable efforts" with benchmarks defined post-contract
Proposed Revision:

  *   Define SLAs upfront, including:
     *   Turnaround time: Target 5 business days per batch (~75 sequences/week)
     *   Throughput: Minimum weekly delivery capacity aligned to ~75 sequences/week
     *   Quality: accuracy thresholds (to be aligned based on training period results)
  *   Replace "commercially reasonable efforts" with measurable, enforceable SLAs
  *   Include service credits or remedies for missed SLAs
3. Benchmarking & Acceptance Criteria
Current: Benchmarks defined after project start
Proposed Revision:

  *   Establish benchmark quality and processing metrics prior to contract execution (these can be defined during the initial training period prior to commencement of the annual contract)
  *   Attach these benchmarks as a contract exhibit
  *   Ensure benchmarks cannot be unilaterally adjusted
4. Acceptance & Rework Terms
Current: 72-hour acceptance window; work deemed accepted thereafter
Proposed Revision:

  *   Extend acceptance window to 5 business days (recognizing internal QA workflows and time zone differences)
  *   Add a latent defect provision (e.g., 30 days) for quality issues not immediately detectable

subject: RE: DBT Tech Showcase at London Tech Week
text:
Hi Leo and team,

I hope you’ve been keeping well.

Following up on the below, I’m very happy to inform you that DBT would like to offer Encord the opportunity to exhibit at DBT’s London Tech Week Showcase. Take a look at the attached Showcase Deck, and follow the process outlined below to RSVP asap.

Drop me any questions you might have, and do cc me so I know that you’ve selected to take up the offer.

Kind regards,
Rohin

As one of the UK’s leading AI companies, DBT would like to offer you a place in our UK Tech Showcase at London Tech Week, held at Olympia during 8 - 10 June.
With 52 companies joining this year’s showcase, our offer includes:

  *   A branded plinth featuring a 24” LED screen, lockable cupboard, USB connector and power supply, available for one day with option for a second, subject to availability. ​
  *   Four full-access exhibitor passes for company representatives, valid on all event days. ​
  *   Entry into our one-to-one meeting programme with DBT’s international delegation of buyers and investors. ​

There is no charge for any of the above, you only need cover travel and accommodation costs. More information on the opportunity can be found in the attached slide deck.

To join us, please contact lpope@brayleinoevents.com<mailto:xxxxxxxx@brayleinoevents.com> by as soon as possible, indicating your preferred first day of participation - Monday, 8th June or Tuesday, 9th June - and whether you’d like to be considered for a second day on Wednesday, 10th June. We’ll provide further logistical information in due course.

If you’re unable to participate, we’d still like you to join us at Olympia and can offer an exhibition pass for one of your team.

We look forward to welcoming you to Olympia in June for an outstanding celebration of UK technology.
